files.mmogr/ggchat/.github/workflows/ci.yml@56:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  # Superseding a push to a branch is the point of this: the older run is
  # testing a commit nobody will merge. A push to `main` is the opposite --
  # it is the only run that tests two PRs together, each of which was green
  # on its own, and there is no later run that repeats the reading, because
  # the next push to main is a different tree again. Measured on
  # 2026-09-07: six merges landed within minutes and cancelled each other,
  # `a199ca3` was the first main run in that window allowed to finish, and
  # it failed.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  format:
    name: Format
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Toolchain
        run: swift --version
      - name: Check formatting
        run: make fmt-check

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install linters
        run: brew install swiftlint actionlint
      - name: Lint Swift and workflows
        run: make lint

  # `swiftlint lint` cannot run the rules under `analyzer_rules`: they need
  # the arguments the compiler was given, so they need a build. Nothing ran
  # them, which made that block in .swiftlint.yml a list of rules that had
  # never once been applied.
  analyze:
    name: Analyze
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install swiftlint
        run: brew install swiftlint
      # No .build cache here on purpose: the analyzer reads the compile
      # commands a build prints, and a cache warm enough to skip compiling
      # would leave it with nothing to read.
      - name: Run the analyzer rules
        run: make analyze

  boundaries:
    name: Check Boundaries
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Check module boundaries
        run: make boundaries

  enforcement:
    name: Enforce Architecture
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Glass sites
        run: scripts/check_glass_sites.sh
      - name: No hand-drawn glass
        run: scripts/check_no_hand_drawn_glass.sh
      - name: Time is an argument
        run: scripts/check_time_is_an_argument.sh
      - name: One writer for the pipe status
        run: scripts/check_one_status_writer.sh
      - name: No print
        run: scripts/check_no_print.sh
      - name: No credential in a log call
        run: scripts/check_log_calls.sh
      - name: File size
        run: scripts/check_file_size.sh
      - name: README claims name their tests
        run: scripts/check_readme_claims.sh
      - name: Test and marker counts have not fallen
        run: scripts/check_test_counts.sh
      - name: make phone picks one iPhone or refuses
        run: scripts/check_phone_device.sh
      # Last, because it needs the network and refuses a tree that pins no
      # release, which every check above can still be read on.
      - name: The vendored gglib binding is the pinned release's
        run: scripts/check_gglib_take.sh

  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # Every package cache is keyed on Package.swift as well: gglib's
      # frameworks are root binary targets pinned there, which Package.resolved
      # never records, so a new pin is a new key and its downloads are saved.
      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .build
          key: spm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Package.resolved', 'Package.swift') }}
          restore-keys: spm-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Toolchain
        run: xcodebuild -version && swift --version
      - name: Build the package with warnings as errors
        run: make build
      # The package in its Release configuration. The app build below also
      # links it in Release, but writes to DerivedData; this is the only one
      # that leaves package objects where the checker looks, and so
      # the only one that can ask whether the DEBUG-only mock pipe is absent
      # from a shipped binary rather than merely unchosen by the factory. Not
      # in the enforcement job: that one runs on Linux and this needs a Swift
      # toolchain and the macOS SDK.
      - name: Build for release and check the mock pipe is not in it
        run: make build-release
      # The xcodebuild invocations live in the Makefile so `make ci` compiles
      # what this job compiles instead of an approximation of it.
      - name: Build the app for macOS and the iOS simulator
        if: hashFiles('App/ggchat.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj') != ''
        run: make build-app
      # Debug is the only configuration anything here had ever compiled: the
      # scheme's run and test actions are Debug, `xcodebuild build` with no
      # -configuration takes the run action's, and the Release archive action
      # is never invoked. So the `#else` arm of every `#if DEBUG` -- the code
      # that decides what a shipped app does -- reached no compiler at all.
      - name: Compile the Release configuration
        if: hashFiles('App/ggchat.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj') != ''
        run: make build-app-release

  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .build
          key: spm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Package.resolved', 'Package.swift') }}
          restore-keys: spm-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Lockfile guard
        run: |
          swift package resolve
          git diff --exit-code Package.resolved
      - name: Run tests with coverage
        run: |
          swift test --parallel --enable-code-coverage --xunit-output test-results.xml
      - name: Export coverage
        run: |
          profdata="$(dirname "$(swift test --show-codecov-path)")/default.profdata"
          binary=.build/debug/ggchatPackageTests.xctest/Contents/MacOS/ggchatPackageTests
          xcrun llvm-cov export -format=lcov -instr-profile "$profdata" "$binary" \
            -ignore-filename-regex='\.build|Tests/' > coverage.lcov
          xcrun llvm-cov report -instr-profile "$profdata" "$binary" \
            -ignore-filename-regex='\.build|Tests/' | tee coverage-summary.txt
      - name: Upload test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: |
            test-results*.xml
            coverage.lcov
            coverage-summary.txt

  uitest:
    name: UI Test (${{ matrix.name }})
    runs-on: macos-26
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The whole walk, then the display settings that only change how it is
        # drawn, over the gallery that photographs every screen. A setting
        # belongs here only when `simctl ui` can both set it and read it back.
        # Reduce Transparency it cannot, so that run carries no setting: the
        # test sets it and measures the consequence itself.
        include:
          - name: iPhone
            slug: iphone
            device: iPhone
            tests: ggchatUITests
            # Skipped here because it has a leg of its own below. Running it
            # in both means running it twice on one device family, and the
            # second one inherits whatever the eighteen tests before it left
            # the simulator in: measured on a199ca3, the dedicated leg passed
            # and this one failed the same test with `Failed to launch
            # com.apple.Preferences: Timed out`. That is not a reading about
            # the app. The iPad leg below skips it too, for an unrelated
            # reason it states there.
            skip: ggchatUITests/ReduceTransparencyUITests
            option: ""
            value: ""
            warm: ""
          - name: iPhone dark
            slug: iphone-dark
            device: iPhone
            tests: ggchatUITests/ScreenGalleryUITests
            skip: ""
            option: appearance
            value: dark
            warm: ""
          - name: iPhone contrast
            slug: iphone-contrast
            device: iPhone
            tests: ggchatUITests/ScreenGalleryUITests
            skip: ""
            option: increase_contrast
            value: enabled
            warm: ""
          - name: iPhone reduce transparency
            slug: iphone-reduce-transparency
            device: iPhone
            tests: ggchatUITests/ReduceTransparencyUITests
            skip: ""
            option: ""
            value: ""
            warm: com.apple.Preferences
          # The walk again on the other device family this app ships for.
          # TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY is "1,2" and the root is a
          # NavigationSplitView, which is a stack on an iPhone and two
          # columns on an iPad: every leg above ran the compact layout, so
          # nothing had ever driven the one an iPad user sees.
          #
          # It skips the Reduce Transparency reading, which is a measurement
          # rather than a walk. Its bands were fractions of an iPhone's
          # screenshot, 0.83-0.94 of the height against a band above it; on
          # an iPad Pro 13-inch both were mostly background and the ratio
          # moved 0.0026 where the test wanted 0.01, a failure about the
          # shape of the screen rather than the app. The bands now come from
          # the composer's own frame (#129), but the reading has been
          # measured on iPhones only, so it stays off this leg until it has
          # been measured here. The iPhone leg above still runs it.
          - name: iPad
            slug: ipad
            device: iPad
            tests: ggchatUITests
            skip: ggchatUITests/ReduceTransparencyUITests
            option: ""
            value: ""
            warm: ""
    env:
      BUNDLE: uitest-${{ matrix.slug }}.xcresult
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # Not the `.build` the other jobs cache: xcodebuild resolves the package
      # into its own cloned-source-packages directory and never reads .build,
      # so caching that here would restore something this job cannot use.
      # This saves the clone, not the compile.
      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .build/xcode-spm
          key: xcode-spm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Package.resolved', 'Package.swift') }}
          restore-keys: xcode-spm-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Pick a booted simulator
        id: sim
        env:
          DEVICE: ${{ matrix.device }}
        run: |
          # Newest runtime first, sorted on a tuple of integers. Sorting the
          # keys as strings would put iOS-9-3 above iOS-18-4, and iOS-26-5
          # above iOS-26-10, which could hand an older runtime's device to an
          # app that needs 26 and draws with .glassEffect.
          # The family is the matrix's, not a constant: with it hard-coded to
          # iPhone the iPad leg would boot an iPhone and pass as a fifth copy
          # of the run above it.
          #
          # An empty family is that same bug wearing a different hat, and it
          # is the one thing here nothing downstream can catch: it matches
          # every name, so a leg added without a `device:` key takes whatever
          # the newest runtime lists first -- an iPhone on this image -- and
          # the name check below, comparing against the same empty string,
          # waves it through. Refused here instead.
          if [ -z "$DEVICE" ]; then
            echo "::error::this leg names no device family"
            exit 1
          fi
          read -r udid name <<<"$(xcrun simctl list devices available --json \
            | python3 -c "import json,os,re,sys;p=os.environ['DEVICE'];d=json.load(sys.stdin)['devices'];v=lambda k:tuple(map(int,re.findall(r'\d+',k)));x=next(x for k in sorted((k for k in d if 'iOS' in k),key=v,reverse=True) for x in d[k] if x['name'].startswith(p));print(x['udid'],x['name'])")"
          # A family the image has no device for: `next` raises, the traceback
          # goes to the log and stdout comes back empty. Named here rather
          # than left to the check below, which would report a leg that "got"
          # a blank device, or to xcodebuild an hour later.
          if [ -z "$udid" ]; then
            echo "::error::no $DEVICE simulator on this runner image"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "this leg runs on $name ($udid)"
          # The name is read back and checked against the family the leg is
          # named for. This is a check on the picker rather than on the
          # simulator, and it cannot fire for a device the picker could pick
          # today: the same $DEVICE filters the list above. What it catches
          # is an edit to that filter -- hard-code the family to iPhone and
          # the iPad leg fails here instead of going green on a layout it
          # never drew.
          case "$name" in
            "$DEVICE"*) ;;
            *) echo "::error::the $DEVICE leg got $name"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "udid=$udid" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Booting a booted device is an error by design, so that stays
          # tolerant. bootstatus is the gate: a simulator that never comes up
          # should fail here, by name, not twenty minutes later inside
          # xcodebuild.
          xcrun simctl boot "$udid" || true
          xcrun simctl bootstatus "$udid" -b
      - name: Set the display setting this run is for
        if: matrix.option != ''
        env:
          UDID: ${{ steps.sim.outputs.udid }}
          OPTION: ${{ matrix.option }}
          VALUE: ${{ matrix.value }}
        run: |
          # simctl exits 117 on an option it does not have and prints what it
          # reads back, so the setting is checked rather than assumed. A
          # runtime that does not support it reads "unsupported", and a bad
          # value for increase_contrast exits 0, so the read-back is the only
          # thing that actually says the mode took.
          xcrun simctl ui "$UDID" "$OPTION" "$VALUE"
          got=$(xcrun simctl ui "$UDID" "$OPTION")
          if [ "$got" != "$VALUE" ]; then
            echo "::error::$OPTION did not take: the simulator reads $got"
            exit 1
          fi
      # Settings' first launch on a simulator that has just booted can take
      # longer than the half minute XCUIApplication.launch() waits for it,
      # and the reduce transparency leg's first act is to open it: on
      # 7faa31b it failed twice running, both times on that first launch,
      # before the app was ever opened. Opened once here, through simctl,
      # which waits for as long as it takes, the test's launch is a warm one.
      - name: Open the app the test drives first, so its launch is warm
        if: matrix.warm != ''
        env:
          UDID: ${{ steps.sim.outputs.udid }}
          WARM: ${{ matrix.warm }}
        run: |
          xcrun simctl launch "$UDID" "$WARM"
          xcrun simctl terminate "$UDID" "$WARM"
      - name: Drive the first-run flow on a simulator
        env:
          UDID: ${{ steps.sim.outputs.udid }}
          TESTS: ${{ matrix.tests }}
          SKIP: ${{ matrix.skip }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          # xcodebuild refuses to write a result bundle that already exists,
          # and a re-run on a warm runner has one.
          rm -rf "$BUNDLE"
          # The legs that skip nothing must pass no -skip-testing: at all,
          # so the flag is built as an array rather than interpolated into
          # the command: an empty `-skip-testing:` is an argument, not the
          # absence of one.
          skip=()
          if [ -n "$SKIP" ]; then skip=(-skip-testing:"$SKIP"); fi
          xcodebuild test -project App/ggchat.xcodeproj -scheme ggchat \
            -destination "id=$UDID" \
            -resultBundlePath "$BUNDLE" \
            -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath .build/xcode-spm \
            -only-testing:"$TESTS" "${skip[@]}" \
            CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES -quiet
      - name: Say which tests ran and why any failed
        if: always()
        run: |
          xcrun xcresulttool get test-results tests --path "$BUNDLE" --format json \
            | python3 -c "
          import json, sys
          cases, failures = [], []
          def walk(nodes, case=None, failing=False):
              for n in nodes:
                  if n.get('nodeType') == 'Test Case':
                      case, result = n.get('name'), n.get('result')
                      failing = result == 'Failed'
                      cases.append((result, case))
                  # A skipped test carries a message too, and the live tests
                  # skip on CI; only a failing one is worth an annotation.
                  if n.get('nodeType') == 'Failure Message' and failing:
                      failures.append((case, n.get('name')))
                  walk(n.get('children', []), case, failing)
          walk(json.load(sys.stdin).get('testNodes', []))
          for result, name in cases:
              print(f'{result}\t{name}')
          for case, message in failures:
              print(f'::error::{case}: {message}')
          if not cases:
              print('::error::no tests ran; the Xcode project is probably stale, run make project')
              sys.exit(1)
          "
      - name: Upload the screenshots it took
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ui-test-screenshots-${{ matrix.slug }}
          path: ${{ env.BUNDLE }}

  unused:
    name: Unused Code
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .build
          key: spm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Package.resolved', 'Package.swift') }}
          restore-keys: spm-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Install periphery
        run: brew install periphery
      - name: Scan
        run: make unused

  docs:
    name: Docs
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .build
          key: spm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Package.resolved', 'Package.swift') }}
          restore-keys: spm-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Build DocC with warnings as errors
        run: make docs
